radiologyTemplates.name: Chest X-Ray (PA View)
radiologyTemplates.technique: Standard erect Postero-Anterior (PA) chest radiograph acquired at full inspiration.

sections.title: Lungs & Hilum
sections.defaultText: Both lung fields are clear and well-expanded. No focal consolidation, cavitation, mass, or interstitial infiltrate seen. Pulmonary hila are normal in size and contour.

sections.title: Cardiomediastinal Silhouette
sections.defaultText: Cardiothoracic ratio is within normal limits (<0.5). Mediastinal contours and aortic knuckle are unremarkable. Trachea is central.

sections.title: Pleura, Diaphragm & Bony Thorax
sections.defaultText: Both costophrenic angles are sharp and clear with no pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Hemidiaphragms are smooth. Visualized ribs, clavicles, and thoracic spine appear intact.

radiologyTemplates.normalImpression: Normal chest radiograph. No active cardiopulmonary abnormality detected.
radiologyTemplates.advice: Correlate clinically. Repeat film if symptoms persist.

quickMacros.label: RLL Pneumonia
quickMacros.findingText: Patchy homogenous airspace opacity with air bronchograms noted in the right lower zone.
quickMacros.impressionText: Right lower zone consolidation — suggestive of lobar pneumonia. Clinical & CBC correlation advised.

quickMacros.label: Mild Cardiomegaly
quickMacros.findingText: Cardiothoracic ratio is mildly enlarged (0.55) with left ventricular contour prominence.
quickMacros.impressionText: Mild cardiomegaly without overt pulmonary edema. 2D Echocardiography advised.

quickMacros.label: Right Pleural Effusion
quickMacros.findingText: Blunting of the right costophrenic angle with homogeneous meniscus opacity tracking up the lateral chest wall.
quickMacros.impressionText: Mild-to-moderate right-sided pleural effusion. USG chest localization recommended.

radiologyTemplates.name: X-Ray KUB (Kidneys, Ureters, Bladder)
radiologyTemplates.technique: Supine AP radiograph of abdomen & pelvis covering renal outlines to pubic symphysis.

sections.title: Renal Outlines & Psoas Shadows
sections.defaultText: Both renal outlines are normal in position and size. Bilateral psoas muscle margins are well-preserved.

sections.title: Radio-opaque Calculi & Bowel Gas
sections.defaultText: No definite radio-opaque calculus is seen along the expected course of the kidneys, ureters, or urinary bladder. Bowel gas pattern is unremarkable.

sections.title: Visualized Skeleton
sections.defaultText: Lumbar vertebrae, sacroiliac joints, and pelvic bones show no acute bony lesion.

radiologyTemplates.normalImpression: No radio-opaque urinary tract calculus identified on plain KUB radiograph.
radiologyTemplates.advice: USG KUB or Non-contrast CT KUB if clinical suspicion of radiolucent stone persists.

quickMacros.label: Right Renal Calculus
quickMacros.findingText: A well-defined ~7 mm radio-opaque density is projected over the right renal fossa.
quickMacros.impressionText: Right renal calculus (~7 mm). Correlate with USG KUB for hydronephrosis.

radiologyTemplates.name: NCCT Head / Brain (Multi-Slice Axial)
radiologyTemplates.technique: Non-contrast contiguous 5 mm axial CT sections from skull base to vertex with multiplanar reconstructions.

sections.title: Brain Parenchyma
sections.defaultText: Cerebral hemispheres, basal ganglia, thalami, brainstem, and cerebellum demonstrate normal attenuation with preserved grey-white matter differentiation. No acute territorial infarct, mass lesion, or midline shift.

sections.title: Ventricles, Cisterns & Extra-axial Spaces
sections.defaultText: Ventricular system and basal cisterns are symmetrical and normal in caliber. No subdural, epidural, or subarachnoid hemorrhage.

sections.title: Calvarium & Paranasal Sinuses
sections.defaultText: Calvarial vault and skull base show no fracture. Visualized mastoid air cells and paranasal sinuses are clear.

radiologyTemplates.normalImpression: Normal non-contrast CT scan of the brain. No acute intracranial hemorrhage or space-occupying lesion.
radiologyTemplates.advice: MRI Brain with DWI/FLAIR recommended if hyperacute ischemia is clinically suspected.

quickMacros.label: Acute ICH (Basal Ganglia)
quickMacros.findingText: Hyperdense acute hematoma (~62 HU) in the left putamen/basal ganglia with mild surrounding vasogenic edema and 3 mm rightward midline shift.
quickMacros.impressionText: CRITICAL: Acute left basal ganglia intraparenchymal hemorrhage with mild mass effect. Urgent neurosurgical evaluation advised.

quickMacros.label: Chronic Lacunar Infarct
quickMacros.findingText: Small chronic hypodense lacunar focus noted in the right corona radiata without surrounding edema.
quickMacros.impressionText: Old right corona radiata lacunar infarct; mild age-related cerebral atrophy.

radiologyTemplates.name: Ultrasound Whole Abdomen & Pelvis
radiologyTemplates.technique: Real-time B-mode and color Doppler transabdominal ultrasonography using 3.5–5.0 MHz curvilinear transducer.
radiologyTemplates.indicationPrompt: Abdominal pain / LFT elevation / Routine health check

sections.title: Liver & Biliary Tree
sections.defaultText: Liver is normal in size and contour with homogeneous parenchymal echotexture. No focal space-occupying lesion. Intrahepatic biliary radicles and CBD are not dilated.

sections.title: Gallbladder, Pancreas & Spleen
sections.defaultText: Gallbladder is well-distended with normal wall thickness; no intraluminal calculus or pericholecystic fluid. Pancreas and spleen appear unremarkable.

sections.title: Kidneys & Urinary Bladder
sections.defaultText: Both kidneys are normal in size, shape, and corticomedullary differentiation without calculus or hydronephrosis. Urinary bladder is well-filled with smooth wall; no free intraperitoneal fluid.

radiologyTemplates.normalImpression: Normal ultrasound study of the whole abdomen and pelvis.

quickMacros.label: Grade I Fatty Liver
quickMacros.findingText: Liver shows mildly increased diffuse parenchymal echogenicity with preserved periportal and diaphragmatic definition.
quickMacros.impressionText: Grade I hepatic steatosis (Fatty Liver). Correlate with LFT & Lipid Profile.

quickMacros.label: Cholelithiasis
quickMacros.findingText: Gallbladder contains a mobile echogenic calculus (~11 mm) casting clean posterior acoustic shadowing; wall thickness normal (2.4 mm).
quickMacros.impressionText: Cholelithiasis without signs of acute cholecystitis.

radiologyTemplates.name: 2D Transthoracic Echocardiography & Color Doppler
radiologyTemplates.technique: 2D, M-mode, Spectral & Color Flow Doppler study via parasternal, apical, and subcostal windows.
radiologyTemplates.indicationPrompt: Chest pain / Dyspnea / Hypertension / Pre-op evaluation

sections.title: Chambers & Ventricular Function
sections.defaultText: All four cardiac chambers are normal in dimensions. Left ventricular systolic function is normal with no regional wall motion abnormality (RWMA). Normal RV systolic excursion.

sections.title: Valves & Color Doppler
sections.defaultText: Mitral, aortic, tricuspid, and pulmonary valves are morphologically thin and pliable with normal excursion. No significant valvular stenosis or regurgitation. Trace physiological TR only.

sections.title: Pericardium & Great Vessels
sections.defaultText: Intact interatrial and interventricular septa. No pericardial effusion, intracardiac thrombus, or vegetation. Normal aortic root and IVC collapsibility.

radiologyTemplates.normalImpression: Normal 2D & Doppler Echocardiography with preserved biventricular systolic function (LVEF 62%).

quickMacros.label: Grade I Diastolic Dysfunction
quickMacros.findingText: Concentric LV remodeling with E/A reversal (<0.8) indicating impaired LV relaxation; preserved systolic LVEF (60%).
quickMacros.impressionText: Concentric LV remodeling with Grade I diastolic dysfunction; good LV systolic function (LVEF 60%).

services.name: Complete Blood Count (Automated 6-Part Hemogram)
services.methodology: Hydrodynamic Focusing & Fluorescent Flow Cytometry (Sysmex XN-1000)

interpretations.normal: Erythroid, myeloid, and megakaryocytic indices are within biological reference intervals. No peripheral cytopenia or leukocytosis detected.
interpretations.abnormalLow: Reduced hematological index detected (anemia, leukopenia, or thrombocytopenia). Recommend peripheral smear correlation and iron/B12 studies.
interpretations.abnormalHigh: Elevated cellular count noted; consider reactive leukocytosis or inflammatory thrombocytosis. Clinical correlation advised.
interpretations.critical: CRITICAL PANIC VALUE ALERT: Immediate physician notification required per critical call protocol.
interpretations.methodologyNote: Assayed on EDTA anticoagulated whole blood via fluorescent flow cytometry.

services.name: Liver Function Panel (Comprehensive Hepatic Profile)
services.methodology: Photometric UV Kinetic & Diazo Colorimetry (Cobas c503)

interpretations.normal: Hepatocellular transaminases and biliary excretion markers lie within normal physiological limits.
interpretations.abnormalLow: Minimally reduced hepatic marker without clinical significance unless associated with chronic insufficiency.
interpretations.abnormalHigh: Elevated transaminases or bilirubin suggestive of hepatocellular injury or cholestasis. Viral serology and USG abdomen advised.
interpretations.critical: CRITICAL HEPATIC INJURY ALERT: Markedly elevated transaminases/hyperbilirubinemia (>10× ULN). Immediate clinician escalation required.
interpretations.methodologyNote: IFCC standardized UV kinetic assay at 37°C.

services.name: Lipid Profile (Atherogenic & Cardiovascular Risk)
services.methodology: Enzymatic Colorimetric Assay (CHOD-PAP / GPO-PAP + Friedewald Formula)

interpretations.normal: Desirable lipid fractions with optimal Total/HDL cholesterol balance and low cardiovascular risk.
interpretations.abnormalLow: Suboptimal HDL cholesterol reduces cardioprotective reverse cholesterol transport. Lifestyle modification advised.
interpretations.abnormalHigh: Dyslipidemia noted (elevated LDL-C and/or hypertriglyceridemia). Stratify 10-year ASCVD risk and evaluate lipid-lowering therapy.
interpretations.critical: CRITICAL HYPERLIPIDEMIA ALERT: Severe hypertriglyceridemia (>1000 mg/dL) carries high risk of acute pancreatitis.
interpretations.methodologyNote: Friedewald formula applied automatically for VLDL & LDL-C.

services.name: Thyroid Function Panel (TSH Ultra-Sensitive, FT3, FT4)
services.methodology: CMIA Chemiluminescent Microparticle Immunoassay (Abbott Alinity i)

interpretations.normal: Euthyroid biochemical profile with intact hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis feedback.
interpretations.abnormalLow: Suppressed TSH or low Free T4 observed. Evaluate for overt/subclinical hyperthyroidism vs central hypothyroidism.
interpretations.abnormalHigh: Elevated TSH or Free T4/FT3 detected. Correlate for primary hypothyroidism or thyrotoxicosis; anti-TPO antibodies advised.
interpretations.critical: CRITICAL ENDOCRINE ALERT: Extreme TSH/FT4 deviation consistent with myxedema coma or thyroid storm risk.

interpretations.normal: Non-diabetic glycemic control (<5.7%) over the preceding 90–120 days.
interpretations.abnormalLow: Low HbA1c (<4.0%) may reflect recurrent hypoglycemia or shortened erythrocyte lifespan.
interpretations.abnormalHigh: Elevated HbA1c: 5.7–6.4% indicates prediabetes; ≥6.5% meets ADA diagnostic threshold for Diabetes Mellitus.
interpretations.critical: CRITICAL HYPERGLYCEMIA HISTORY: HbA1c >12.0% denotes severe poorly controlled diabetes.

services.name: Renal Function Test (KFT & eGFR)
services.methodology: Enzymatic Creatininase & Urease GLDH UV (Cobas c503)

reagentBom.reagentName: Cobas Creatinine Plus & Urea Kinetic Pack

interpretations.normal: Preserved glomerular filtration rate and normal nitrogenous waste clearance.
interpretations.abnormalLow: Reduced eGFR (<90 mL/min/1.73m²). Evaluate hydration status and uACR for CKD staging.
interpretations.abnormalHigh: Azotemia / elevated creatinine or hyperuricemia. Differentiate prerenal dehydration from intrinsic renal impairment.
interpretations.critical: CRITICAL RENAL DYSFUNCTION ALERT: Markedly elevated creatinine (>5.0 mg/dL) or eGFR <15.

interpretations.abnormalLow: Fasting hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL). Correlate with insulinoma workup or antihyperglycemic dosing.
interpretations.abnormalHigh: 100–125 mg/dL indicates Impaired Fasting Glucose; ≥126 mg/dL on two occasions supports Diabetes Mellitus.
interpretations.critical: CRITICAL GLYCEMIC ALERT: Severe hypoglycemia (<45 mg/dL) or hyperglycemic crisis (>450 mg/dL). Immediate intervention required.
interpretations.methodologyNote: Hexokinase G-6-PDH reference enzymatic method on NaF/K-oxalate plasma.

interpretations.normal: No acute systemic inflammatory response detected (<5.0 mg/L).
interpretations.abnormalHigh: Elevated CRP indicates active acute-phase inflammation, bacterial infection, or tissue injury. Correlate with CBC and procalcitonin.
interpretations.critical: CRITICAL INFLAMMATION ALERT: Markedly elevated CRP (>150 mg/L) suggestive of severe sepsis or systemic inflammatory syndrome.

interpretations.normal: Vitamin D sufficiency (30–100 ng/mL) supporting optimal calcium homeostasis and bone mineralization.
interpretations.abnormalLow: Vitamin D deficiency (<20 ng/mL) or insufficiency (20–29 ng/mL). Cholecalciferol supplementation and serum calcium/PTH review advised.
interpretations.abnormalHigh: Elevated 25-OH Vitamin D (>100 ng/mL); evaluate for hypervitaminosis D and monitor serum calcium.
interpretations.critical: CRITICAL VITAMIN D TOXICITY / SEVERE DEFICIENCY: Immediate endocrinology & bone metabolism review advised.
interpretations.methodologyNote: Competitive chemiluminescent immunoassay measuring D2 + D3.

interpretations.normal: Physicochemical, dipstick qualitative analytes, and microscopic sediment parameters are within normal reference limits.
interpretations.abnormalLow: Hyposthenuria / low specific gravity; correlate with hydration or renal concentrating ability.
interpretations.abnormalHigh: Abnormal dipstick finding (proteinuria, glycosuria, ketonuria, or positive nitrite) or pyuria/hematuria detected. Correlate clinically and consider urine C/S.
interpretations.critical: CRITICAL URINALYSIS FINDING: Marked proteinuria/glycosuria (+4) or gross pyuria/hematuria requiring urgent clinical review.
interpretations.methodologyNote: 10-parameter dipstick reflectance photometry confirmed by centrifuged sediment microscopy at 400×.
